study.title: Towards clinical translation of deep-learning based classification of DSA image sequences for stroke treatment

imaging.modality_detail: DSA sequences (frontal and lateral) acquired during thrombectomy; test cases on Siemens ARTIS icono biplane, training data on Siemens ARTIS zee biplane
imaging.territory_detail: Middle cerebral artery (M1-M3) and carotid terminus occlusions in acute ischemic stroke

data_released.detail: Application and trained model released; data release not stated

task.task_description: Open-source client-server tool classifying whole DSA sequences as thrombus-free vs non-thrombus-free using retrained EfficientNetV2+GRU models (frontal and lateral, predictions averaged); evaluated on functionality, correctness on three new clinical cases from a different DSA system, and runtime across hardware.
task.clinical_application: Detection of remaining thrombi during mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke

temporal_evidence.quote: One network setup that yielded good results in [6] is EfficentNetV2+GRU. We employ this architecture for classification

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Three new physician-selected cases (pre- and post-treatment sequences) acquired with a Siemens ARTIS icono biplane, a different angiography unit than the training data (Siemens ARTIS zee biplane)
